cipher.name: Base64 encoding
cipher.idea: A deterministic reversible encoding that converts the UTF-8 byte representation of the plaintext into Base64. The plaintext is first encoded as UTF-8 bytes, and those bytes are then represented using the standard Base64 alphabet consisting of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, '+', and '/'. Padding with '=' is added when required. This transformation operates on bytes rather than individual letters and does not preserve the original punctuation, whitespace, or letter case structure in the encoded representation.
cipher.encrypt_rules: First encode the entire plaintext string into bytes using UTF-8. Then encode the resulting byte sequence using standard Base64 as defined by the alphabet ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/. Process the input bytes in groups of three bytes (24 bits), divide each group into four 6-bit values, and map each value to the corresponding Base64 character. If the final group contains fewer than three bytes, use '=' characters as standard Base64 padding. Return the resulting Base64 string without adding extra whitespace or line breaks.
cipher.decrypt_rules: Decode the Base64 string using the standard Base64 alphabet ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/. Interpret each group of four Base64 characters as the corresponding encoded bytes, respecting '=' padding at the end of the string. Reconstruct the original byte sequence and decode those bytes using UTF-8 to recover the exact original plaintext.
